description: Executable state-preservation corpus. Each observation is bound to the repository's own reference test cases on both the Rust source side (/input/source) and the Go target side (/input/target). Both sides must report PASS; the normalized common projection is the status wrapper {"result": "PASS"}.

projection.normalization: Both sides emit the stable wrapper {"result": "PASS"} (or {"result": "FAIL"} on failure). The wrapper is identical after normalization, so source and target compare equal.

observations.atomic_claim: SyncHTTPClient.Call(HTTPRequest) (HTTPResponse, error) and AsyncHTTPClient.Call(ctx, HTTPRequest) (HTTPResponse, error) are the single call operations carrying method/URL/headers/body and returning status/headers/body or error, and a caller-supplied implementation passed to Request/RequestAsync is the one invoked.
The migrated package retains every public capability of the Rust library and continues to implement the RFC 6749, RFC 7662, RFC 7009 and RFC 8628 semantics without behavioral change.

NewBasicClient(NewClientId("id")) defaults AuthType to BasicAuth; each of SetAuthURL, SetTokenURL, SetRedirectURL, SetDeviceAuthorizationURL, SetIntrospectionURL, SetRevocationURL and SetClientSecret stores its value with the matching accessor returning it, and the conditional Set*URLOption setters accept an optional endpoint while flow accessors are fallible.

A status-200 response with a non-empty JSON body containing access_token, token_type, optional expires_in, optional refresh_token, optional space-delimited scope and extra fields deserializes into the corresponding token or introspection response with each field populated.
A revocation request inspects only the status code: a body is ignored, a non-200 status is mapped through the status check, and a 200 status returns a nil error.

Executing any flow request through a fake client yields an HTTPRequest with Method "POST", Header["Content-Type"] == "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", Header["Accept"] == "application/json", and a form-encoded body.
Deserializing token_type "BEARER" and "bearer" both yields BasicTokenTypeBearer, and serializing BasicTokenTypeBearer emits "bearer".

The public configuration and error contract surface (AuthUrl, TokenUrl, RedirectUrl, IntrospectionUrl, RevocationUrl, DeviceAuthorizationUrl, ConfigurationError, RequestTokenError, HTTPClientError, BasicAuth/RequestBody, StandardErrorResponse) keeps equivalent names and behavior rebuilt with Go idioms.

fmt.Sprintf with %s, %v and %#v (or String/GoString) of NewClientSecret("s3cr3t"), NewAccessToken, NewRefreshToken, NewAuthorizationCode, NewPkceCodeVerifier, NewCsrfToken, NewDeviceCode, NewUserCode and NewVerificationUriComplete never contains the underlying value, while Secret() returns it.

AddExtraParam(name, value) on the authorization, code, client-credentials, password, refresh-token, device-authorization, device-access-token, introspection and revocation requests appends the supplied name/value to the outgoing request.

Device access token polling calls the supplied sleep function between polls with the device-authorization interval (defaulting to 5s), reuses the same interval on authorization_pending, adds 5s on slow_down, backs off exponentially to a 10s cap (or SetMaxBackoffInterval) on transport errors, and returns an expired_token server-response error once the timeout elapses.

StandardErrorResponse always serializes the required error field and includes error_description and error_uri only when set; token types parse case-insensitively and serialize to canonical strings; error types serialize to their canonical strings.
RevokeToken sends token=<token secret> plus the optional token_type_hint (access_token or refresh_token) and a non-HTTPS revocation URL returns a configuration error.

A non-200 response with a parseable body returns RequestTokenError{Kind: RequestTokenErrorServerResponse}; a non-200 response with an unparseable non-empty body returns Kind RequestTokenErrorParse with RawBody equal to the body; a non-200 response with an empty body returns Kind RequestTokenErrorOther.

AuthorizationRequest.URL() always contains response_type, client_id and state; contains code_challenge and code_challenge_method only when a PKCE challenge is set; contains redirect_uri only when a redirect URL is set; contains scope (space-joined) only when scopes exist; and appends extra parameters, with default response_type=code, UseImplicitFlow selecting token, and SetResponseType supporting a custom value.

A response whose present Content-Type is not application/json after case-insensitive comparison and ignoring parameters returns an other error naming the content type, and a response with an empty body returns an other error reporting an empty body.
RevokeToken with a non-HTTPS revocation URL returns a *ConfigurationError with Kind ConfigurationInsecureURL and the injected HTTP client is never called.

Any flow accessor whose required endpoint is unset returns a *ConfigurationError with Kind ConfigurationMissingURL naming that endpoint (authorization, token, device authorization, introspection or revocation) rather than issuing a request.

A consumer importing package oauth2 can construct a client, build and execute every documented flow request, introspect and revoke tokens, inject a custom HTTP client, and receive the documented response and error types.

With BasicAuth and a client secret the request carries Authorization: Basic base64(urlencode(client_id):urlencode(client_secret)) and omits client_id/client_secret from the body; with RequestBody auth (or no secret) client_id, and client_secret when set, appear in the form body instead.
For each scenario exercised by the Rust unit tests and doctests under oauth2/src using an injected fake HTTP client, the Go implementation produces the same observable request, response or error.
For a fixed input the generated authorization URL matches the baseline tests' exact parameter set, percent-encoding and ordering.
